# bugs #2893: Warning about an empty translation unit before the syntax error when the first token of a file is invalid

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2893/

- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply the patch and close.
- Patch: [bugs-2893.patch](../../patches/bugs-2893.patch), commit [`1d35eb666`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/1d35eb666ce7a32d4a87559b3ef7700186350907). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.

```diff
diff --git a/src/SDCC.y b/src/SDCC.y
index 95b6cc650..b91962c44 100644
--- a/src/SDCC.y

    : /* empty */
      {
-       werror(W_EMPTY_TRANSLATION_UNIT);
+       /* The parser also reduces by this rule when the first token cannot begin a translation unit, and it reports the syntax error afterwards. */
+       if (yychar == YYEOF)
+         werror(W_EMPTY_TRANSLATION_UNIT);
      }
    | translation_unit
    ;
```

## Finding

When the first token of a source file is `;`, the compiler gives two messages. The first is
`warning 190: ISO C forbids an empty translation unit`, and the second is the syntax error for the
semicolon. The file is not empty, so the warning is wrong. Declarations after the semicolon do not
change the result, and files that start with `}` get the warning as well.

This was reproduced on r17176 for mcs51 with the default standard, with `--std-c99`, with
`--std-c23`, and with `--model-large --stack-auto`, and for z80. Empty files and files that
contain only a `#define` get the warning alone, which is correct.

## Cause

The rule `file` in `src/SDCC.y` has an empty alternative, and its action calls
`werror (W_EMPTY_TRANSLATION_UNIT)` without a condition. In the parser that bison generates, this
alternative is the default reduction of the initial state. The parser reduces by it, and runs the
action, for every first token that cannot begin an external declaration. It reports the syntax
error afterwards.

[r13845](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/13845/), which a maintainer names in the ticket's
comment, renamed the warning from "empty source file" to "empty translation unit". It did not
change the rule.

## Fix

The action gives the warning only when the lookahead token `yychar` is `YYEOF`. The initial state
has shift actions for the tokens that begin a declaration, so the parser has read the lookahead
token when it reduces there. The syntax error for the first token stays, which the reporter calls
correct.

## Verification

`support/valdiag/tests/bug-2893.c` has four cases. The first two start with `;` and with `}` and
must get an error. `valdiag.py` does not report additional messages for lines that are marked for
a message, so these two cases pass without the patch too. The third case starts with the token
`'unreferenced function argument'` on a line that is not marked. `valdiag.py` ignores messages
that contain this text. The syntax error is such a message, and the warning is not. The fourth
case checks that a translation unit of comments and directives still gets the warning.

Without the patch, the third case fails on r17192 for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80,
and stm8. With the patch, the four cases pass for them.

With the patch series of this report up to the patch for local 0001 applied to r17192, the
regression suite ran without a failure for host, stm8, ucz80, and mcs51 with the small, medium,
large, and huge models and with `--stack-auto` for the small and large models. The diagnostics
suite ran without a failure for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.

## Related

Files that contain only characters that the lexer rejects, such as one `@`, get error 329 and
then warning 190. The lexer skips the characters, and the parser gets the end of the input as its
first token. The patch does not change this.
